Things a new player should know?

Follow the story line, it's interesting and it's your fastest way to 50 and beyond.

Ask around here about servers, there are probably good folks who would love to invite you to their Free Company (FFXIV Guild Equivalent).

Starting Jobs determine where you first land on the map, that may or may not come into play for you. Gridania is so nice though.
Everyone keeps saying to follow the story, since that's the fastest way to level. roughly how long/how many hours does it take to get a character to 50?
It really depends on how long you are willing to play at one stretch. I couldn't devote a lot of hours days to it so it took me a few weeks.

As everyone has said, keep sticking to the main story. 9 out of 10 questions you have about new areas, dungeons, game mechanics can be answered by saying, "It's unlocked through the story."

As u/d23 mentioned, queues can be brutal as a DPS looking to do dungeons. Right now is a great time though because a new Tank and Healer class has just been introduced. Queues are popping like crazy for everyone!

Don't sell your beginners gear!!! If you want to try out a new class, you will be naked for 5 levels lol. This really isn't a big deal because you can buy it again, but you can just hold onto it in your bank as well.

Be honest about being new when running dungeons. No one is going to care and people will appreciate knowing ahead of time that they need to explain fights.

HAVE FUN! This game leaves a lot open for your own decision in how your story progresses. Don't stress about it too much and enjoy the game! If you end up on Leviathan, send me a PM!

A surprising number of gameplay features and other things are locked behind quests, from the ability to use materia and dye your gear different colors, core class/job abilities, and entire optional dungeons. [Questions] Trying to Find a Starting Point

The easiest way in my opinion is to start with a game that you know really well. This allows you to think less about the gameplay and focus more on talking about what's going on. For me the best mix was to be a little informative, but also give running commentary/reaction on what was going on as well.

 

Be sure to take the game length into consideration though - because you don't want your first LP to be two episodes, but also don't want to be stuck with something that will take 200, since you'll be constantly improving through the first few episodes. Maybe do a short test run of some game that you don't want to LP, and record/render it just like you're planning to for your first LP - so you can catch any big quality issues before you start. Re-recording the same game can ruin the experience.

 

Keep in mind though, you're always going to have flaws so don't try to get it perfect, just pretty decent. You have to start somewhere, so once it's decent just post it and try to improve more as you go.

 

My main advice is to treat the viewer as someone watching over your shoulder, and tell them what's going on in your head. They don't know what your plan is, so don't just go running off randomly - tell them why or where you're going. Make them feel like they know where the adventure is supposed to be going, even if events pop up that throw it off course.

 

As far as being introverted, there's no reason to be shy - just imagine you're talking to your one best friend. If you're really interested and engaged with something, you just need to convey that passion so that the person watching is as well.

 

Hopefully that helps with some of your questions :)

15-30 minutes, just find a good level/break spot and cut the video there - don't try to keep them all the exact same length.

I know some people like to record intros/outros live for each episode (using a timer), but I'd recommend just recording 2-3 hours of gameplay and then breaking it up at appropriate points when you're editing. You can add intro/outros during the editing, or record them when you start and end recording and then copy them into each of the videos if it's just a generic greeting.

It sounds complicated but it's really a simple copy/paste job. As long as you're choosing logical split points it won't seem out of place.

When people say "America is a Republic, not a Democracy" what exactly do they mean? Those terms don't seem to be contradictory.

A Republic is a form of government where people elect a representative to make laws for them. Democracy is purely based off of majority rules. A republic protects the minority while a democracy doesn't.

This is almost all I remember from high school government.

A republic is a representative democracy typically. A democracy is where you and I would all vote on legislation but that is unreasonable for the sake of amendments and points of order alone so we elect representatives to vote for us.

A republic allows for multiple groups to hold power - like Voat - but the democracy is like reddit - a hivemind.

They are not contradictory. When people say this they are normally confused about what a republic is.

If a country is a republic that merely means that the government rules with the consent of the people, or claims to. Even a diret democracy is also a republic, since it is the people who have control of the country.

Normally when people say this they either are repeating something they heard or they mean that the US isn't a direct democracy, which some folks see as the only "real" democracy.

All of the other answers are close, but incorrect. A republic - like ours - can be a form of democracy. And a democracy - like ours - can be a form of a republic. A republic is a form of government that has a set of laws limiting the powers of the government. In the United States, our constitution defines the government's powers and its limitations. At the same time, we have the power to amend the constitution by vote; elect our leaders; etc. So we are a republican democracy. On the other hand, we are not a direct democracy (few, if any societies ever are). A direct democracy (a/k/a pure democracy) is a society governed by the will of the majority, without any limitation. Its utilitarianism in its unadulterated form, with no checks or balances. So, in a pure democracy, if a majority of people voted to sacrifice a left-handed people, no law would prevent them from doing that.
It is a Republic because you do not directly vote for President or the laws of the land. We elect people to go and do that for us.
